analysis.title: The 720: US Midterms, Kioxia, Xiaomi, China DCs, Murata, Yum China, UOB downgrade, Goodman, Fositek
key_insights: US midterms: GS (Hatzius) says Democrats won both the House and the Senate by margins well above expectations. GS expects them to use upcoming fiscal and debt limit deadlines to seek concessions such as limiting the war with Iran, rolling back selected tariffs and reversing last year's spending cuts.
GS estimates the reversal of spending cuts would add 0.25% of GDP to 2027 spending. Federal AI regulation is unlikely to change.
Democratic gubernatorial gains are likely to trigger short-term data center moratoria pending new state legislation. This could affect 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion.

UOB downgraded to Sell from Neutral, 12m TP cut to S$35.1. Q3 net interest margin compression was worse than expected on retail deposit competition and CASA-to-FD migration. A heavier investment cycle raises the risk of negative jaws.
UOB: rising Greater China real estate and hospitality NPLs and falling reserve coverage leave less buffer. FY26E-FY28E net profit estimates were cut by 6% to 13%.

Kioxia stays Buy with 12m TP of ¥39,000 and earnings forecasts changed by under 1%. Recent guidance missed expectations. Management expects Q4 bit growth of high-single-digits to 10% sequentially on data center and enterprise demand.

Kioxia: multi-year contract coverage is substantially above 50% for 2027 and 2028. GS sees a high likelihood of added buybacks in Q4 or fiscal 2028 and says tightening NAND supply supports margins after the share price correction.

Murata (Buy, on the Conviction List) keeps its ¥13,200 TP. GS reads the ¥1 tn MLCC capacity plan as a catalyst for general price hikes across more applications, similar to the 2017 auto electrification cycle. Customer price talks could occur this fiscal year with earnings impact from FY3/28.

Yum China stays Buy with TPs of US$60 (ADR) and HK$467 (H-share). Management guides to double-digit 2027 EPS growth on only 0-2% same-store sales growth, using 10% to low-teens net new-store growth, margin gains and buybacks. Store rental ratios fell below 8% for the first time in nearly a decade.

Xiaomi stays Buy but TP is cut to HK$35, with 2026E-28E revenue cut 0-8% and adjusted net profit cut 6-16% on lower EV revenue and higher AI investment. GS models Q3 revenue down 6% y/y to Rmb107bn and adjusted net profit down 57% to Rmb4.9bn, and expects this to be the trough.

China data centers: GS expects growth and returns to diverge between powered-shell operators and integrated AIDC/neocloud platforms. It raises 2027E-28E EBITDA for Range Intelligent by 150-217% and cuts ADR TPs by 50% on average on wider US-China yield gaps and multiple contraction.

China data centers: Sinnet stays Sell (TP Rmb9) after 2026-28E net income cuts of 42-45% on pricing pressure. Athub and SUNeVision stay Neutral. Buy-rated GDS and VNET carry TPs of US$30/HK$29 and US$4.6.

Goodman Group stays Buy with A$32 TP after a Q1 FY27 update that reiterated 9% FY27 operating EPS growth. No new data centre contracts were announced, so work-in-progress stayed flat at A$19.7bn. FY27E-29E EBITDA and EPS were cut 0.6% to 0.7%.

Fositek stays Buy and TP rises to NT$2,390 from NT$2,082. Q3 revenue missed GS estimates but gross margin beat by 6.4ppt to 38.0%. Vera Rubin needs 25%+ more quick disconnect usage than GB300, and QD capacity is expanding to 4.5mn units a month.

Coupang (Buy) TP raised to $29 after Q3 constant-currency revenue grew 11% y/y and adjusted EBITDA margin was 1.2%. GS sees growth and margin troughs behind. Developing Offerings loss guidance was raised by $50-100 million.
Astellas (Buy, TP ¥3,100): 1H core operating profit was ¥424.9 bn against GS's ¥406.7 bn, driven by Xtandi and Padcev. FY3/27 core operating profit guidance was raised to ¥700 bn from ¥620 bn.

NTT (Buy, TP ¥191): Q2 operating profit of ¥404.9 bn missed GS estimates. Full-year operating profit guidance was raised from ¥1.71 tn to ¥1.73 tn, the first upward revision in nearly five years, and is still below consensus.

Sumitomo Bakelite (Buy, TP ¥11,760): Q2 business profit beat at ¥14.5bn, up 79% y/y. Full-year business profit guidance was raised from ¥38.0bn to ¥55.0bn on semiconductor encapsulation demand from AI servers, memory and LEO satellites.

PayPay (Buy, TP $31): Q2 beat and second guidance raise this year. Take rate rose 10 basis points sequentially and online GMV grew 40% y/y. GS expects temporary Q3 margin pressure from tighter online payment controls.
Shengyi Tech (Buy, TP Rmb255): order visibility runs through 2028 and CCL pricing keeps rising on tight raw materials. The company plans about 25% more rigid PCB CCL capacity over 10-12 months.

APAC Healthcare Corporate Day notes: GenFleet (Buy, TP HK$52) showed dose-dependent safety for GFH276 with zero Grade 3+ rash at 40-120mg in PDAC and a 41% objective response rate in 2L+ PDAC. Gushengtang (TP HK$35.3), Everest Medicines (Neutral, TP HK$39.66), Edge Medical (Buy, TP HK$60) and China Medical System (TP HK$17.96) also covered.

XGimi upgraded to Neutral from Sell, TP raised to Rmb101 from Rmb86. Overseas sales more than doubled to over 60% of revenue and total sales returned to double-digit growth for the first time since late 2022. Memory chip costs and weak domestic demand remain drags.

APAC strategy: October consensus earnings rose 3.3% m/m and GS expects moderately stronger upgrades, led by Taiwan and Korea on memory prices and tech exports. It expects downgrades in China and Australia (iron ore). Preferred long sectors are Tech Hardware, Industrials, Energy and Banks. Short sectors are Utilities, Consumer Discretionary, New Tech and Consumer Staples.

Estee Lauder stays Buy (on the Conviction List) with a $129 TP. FY30 targets from the China Capital Markets Day are mid-single-digit organic sales growth, 16.5%-18.5% adjusted operating margins and double-digit adjusted EPS growth.

ARM (Sell, TP $160): revenue of $1.44 bn and operating EPS of $0.52 beat Street. Licensing of $773 mn was strong but royalties missed at $670 mn. FY Q3 guidance is revenue $1.54 bn and EPS $0.56 at the midpoint, broadly in line.

Freeport-McMoRan (Buy, TP $83): the $4.5bn Bagdad expansion FID was in line. It adds about 225mn lbs of copper a year by mid-2030 and cuts long-term unit net cash costs by roughly 20%. Capex steps up about $0.9bn in 2027 and $1.35-1.58bn in 2028.

NTT Q2 reported: operating profit ¥404.9 bn, below GS expectations. Full-year operating profit guidance raised to ¥1.73 tn from ¥1.71 tn, below consensus.
Sumitomo Bakelite Q2 reported: business profit ¥14.5bn, up 79% y/y. Full-year business profit guidance raised to ¥55.0bn from ¥38.0bn.
PayPay fiscal Q2 reported: beat expectations and raised full-year operating revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance for the second time this year.
